title: LC-MT371-MigrationReplayRecoveryAndParity
clause: Migrate, replay and recover the complete Locus project forest while proving semantic parity and eliminating SQL-era paths.

scope.summary: GOAL: Close the Locus semantic migration against the MT-361 parity matrix. Build fresh SurrealDB initialization and explicit supported-source migration/reconstruction for retained project evidence; do not connect to PostgreSQL or SQLite at runtime. Replay EventLedger state and rebuild taskboards, rollups, Loom relations, query indexes, subscriptions and occupancy projections. Prove restart, backup/restore, corruption detection, partial projection failure and recovery across a representative managed-project forest. Remove all legacy authority adapters, features, fixtures and false-green tests.
forbidden_paths: Runtime connection to or import from SQLite/PostgreSQL
Tests that skip-as-green when SurrealDB is unavailable
Treating logs, UI or projections as recovery authority
acceptance_criteria: Every preserve item in the MT-361 parity matrix has implementation and real-runtime proof; every rejected item has approved rationale and no connected code path.
Fresh SurrealDB initialization creates the complete Locus project-forest schema, indexes, permissions and rollout state without SQLite/PostgreSQL dependencies.
EventLedger replay and canonical reconciliation deterministically rebuild taskboards, rollups, Loom links, query state and recoverable execution projections after restart or projection loss.
Backup/restore and corruption tests preserve project-qualified identity, graph edges, lifecycle revisions, permissions, ledger ordering, leases and idempotency receipts.
Independent dependency/source scans find zero unclassified Locus SQLite/PostgreSQL authority, adapter, fallback, fixture or proof paths.
proof_targets: EventLedger replay plus independent canonical reread
Compile/dependency/source tripwires for SQL-era Locus paths

enforcement_boundaries: Replay and restore preserve original scopes and never default a missing scope to global.
Privacy is re-proven with authenticated users after restore.
same_project_private_resource_cases: Restored private AccessSpace records remain hidden from unauthorized users in the same project.
cross_account_negative_cases: Backups, replay and restore cannot import, enumerate or expose another account's records without explicit authorized scope.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: Rebuilt taskboards, rollups, Loom links, indexes and diagnostics cannot widen restored canonical scopes.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: Revoked identities remain revoked after replay/restore; switching restore target requires fresh authorization and scope validation.
metadata_side_channel_cases: Recovery diagnostics redact private content, secrets, hidden project names/counts and machine-local credential paths.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Record rollout, replay, reconciliation, backup, restore, corruption and legacy-tripwire outcomes.
Expose schema drift, replay gaps, hash mismatch, projection divergence and legacy dependency hits.
Record DEFERRED-with-reason if continuous replay/divergence watchers are unavailable; never silently skip.

risk_if_missed: Locus may appear migrated while capabilities, privacy or recovery remain dependent on stale SQL-era behavior.

risks: A skipped test is reported green.
Replay restores projections but not canonical state.
A legacy adapter survives behind a feature.
minimum_controls: Real managed SurrealDB required for proof.

research_provenance.source: MT-361 parity audit; MT-336 replay/projection contract; MT-362 and MT-366..370 implementation contracts; official SurrealDB rollout, export/import, transaction and permission documentation.
research_provenance.selected_approach: Fresh Surreal authority with deterministic EventLedger replay, repairable projections and exhaustive legacy-path removal.
